text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before any human review. It catches 80% of trivial issues—linting, test coverage gaps, and obvious bugs—freeing humans to focus on design and edge cases. The trade-off is slower feedback for developers who must wait for the automated check to pass before proceeding.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 80% catch rate is a red herring—it normalizes mediocrity by teaching teams to rubber-stamp its output instead of thinking. The real risk is that humans abdicate judgment, turning reviews into a checkbox exercise where only the *objective* (linting, coverage) gets attention while the *meaningful* (design flaws, subtle bugs) slips through. A better alternative: gate PR-Agent for *only* the trivial, non-controversial checks (e.g., linting), then route the rest to humans with a *summary* of PR-Agent’s findings—this keeps humans accountable for the hard calls. Settle it by measuring *post-merge defect rates* and *review time per meaningful comment* before and after the change.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run PR-Agent as a gatekeeper but only for *objective* issues—linting, test cover, and style violations. Humans still own subjective judgment: design, edge cases, and trade-offs. The trade-off is slower feedback for developers who must wait for the automated check to pass before proceeding, but it prevents humans from rubber-stamping mediocre fixes. This keeps the review process rigorous without letting automation dictate quality.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: PR-Agent as a gatekeeper for *objective* issues still outsources judgment to a tool that can’t contextualize trade-offs—it’ll flag "style violations" in code that’s objectively better but violates arbitrary rules. The real risk is that teams conflate *objective* with *trivial*, letting the tool set the floor while humans ignore the ceiling. Settle it by measuring whether the tool’s output correlates with fewer *real* regressions, not just more green checks.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Gate PR-Agent on *only* high-confidence mechanical checks—linting, dependency hygiene, and hard-fail test coverage—with humans reviewing everything else.

Result must deliver: A clear policy artifact (one page max) listing the exact checks PR-Agent enforces, the rationale for each, and the human review scope. Owns it: Gauge.
